THE BUDDHIST PATH · TRAVEL NOTES

One journey.
Four significant places.

Bodh Gaya, Sarnath, Kushinagar and Lumbini each hold a different place in the story of the Buddha.

Read the story ↓
01 / PILGRIMAGE

4 MIN READ

Understanding the four places of pilgrimage

The Buddhist circuit is more than a sequence of landmarks. Its most significant places connect the story of the Buddha’s birth, enlightenment, first teaching and Mahaparinirvana across present-day India and Nepal.

Continue reading

Lumbini: a beginning

In Nepal, Lumbini is recognised as the Buddha’s birthplace. The sacred area around Maya Devi Temple offers a starting point for understanding its significance.

Bodh Gaya: enlightenment

The Mahabodhi Temple complex marks the place associated with the Buddha’s enlightenment. Its setting remains a living place of pilgrimage, prayer and reflection.

Sarnath: the first teaching

Near Varanasi, Sarnath is associated with the Buddha’s first sermon. Stupas and archaeological remains help visitors connect the landscape with the early teaching tradition.

Kushinagar: reflection

Traditionally associated with the Buddha’s Mahaparinirvana, Kushinagar is an important stop for pilgrims contemplating the final chapter of his life.

You do not need to see every place in one trip. Start with the time you have and allow enough room for rest and reflection between travel days.

Further reading: UNESCO: Lumbini, UNESCO: Mahabodhi, IRCTC Buddhist Circuit.

02 / MINDFUL TRAVEL

3 MIN READ

A thoughtful first visit to a Buddhist site

A little preparation helps you settle into the pace of a sacred place. Arrive with curiosity, dress considerately, and allow time to observe.

Continue reading

Let the place guide your pace

Pause before entering an active prayer area. Keep your voice low and give worshippers space. Each monastery or temple has its own customs, so follow posted guidance and ask when unsure.

Ask before you photograph

Photography may be restricted in particular areas. Check local rules, and ask permission before photographing people, ceremonies or private spaces.

Prepare for the practical details

Wear clothing that covers shoulders and knees, carry water for the journey, and choose footwear that is easy to remove where required. Check current opening arrangements and entry restrictions for the sites on your route.

Leave room for stillness

You do not need to practise Buddhism to visit respectfully. A few quiet minutes can be as memorable as a long sightseeing list. Keep the surroundings clean and follow the instructions of site staff.

03 / ON THE ROAD

3 MIN READ

Planning your pilgrimage around your people

The best route is one your whole group can enjoy. Start with comfort, travel time and the experience you want to share.

Continue reading

Begin with your must-visit places

Choose the sites that matter most to your group before deciding how many stops to include. A shorter itinerary with unhurried visits can be more rewarding than covering every destination.

Make comfort part of the plan

Tell your organiser about luggage, walking preferences and any mobility needs. Confirm seating, road travel time and rest stops when choosing a vehicle.

Agree what is included

Ask for a written quotation that clearly sets out transport, guide services, accommodation where requested and additional charges. Confirm payment and cancellation terms before booking.

Plan international stops early

If Lumbini is part of the journey, discuss the border crossing in advance. Check official entry requirements for your nationality and confirm that the transport arrangements cover the proposed route.
